provenance.author: block writer B2 (Claude Opus 5.5, model-written)
notes: Beat as revised: the rain (glaw is not taught until 21, so: water dripping from the old roof) forces Myrddin to lock his things in the leather-bound chest, and he has forgotten where the key is. Wrong objects, each with a comic consequence: quill (Cai), watch (Dafi claims it), spare spectacles (Mali walks into the cupboard and releases a mouse), wheel (rolls away, Pero chases), hand mirror (Cai admires himself), umbrella (bangs open, Cai lands in the cauldron, but it keeps the books dry). The key falls out of the umbrella. The chest's mirror shows Mali the sword in the stone in a white, cold world (eira is not taught until 17).

hyn / hynny are used separately as the block plan asks: after a plural noun (y pethau hyn, y pethau hynny) and abstract (Beth yw hyn? Mae hyn yn rhyfedd; Dw i ddim yn deall hynny; Dw i ddim yn credu hynny). Gender drives hwn / hon (Mali corrects Cai and Arth: 'Pluen yw hon', 'Hon, Arth: allwedd yw hi').
y rhain is counted by the checker only in the literal sequence 'y rhain', so it appears after ar / dan (ar y rhain, dan y rhain); 'Dyw'r rhain …' is used once as well.

Recall: the chapter deliberately reuses Penodau 11–14 words (crochan, llwy, cyllell, torri, cwympo, glanhau, digwydd, gweiddi; inc, plu, ddoe, anghofio, cwestiwn, dyddiadur, teimlo; to, disgyn, cyrraedd, gadael, troi, glanio, lledr, llygoden, nyth, cymylau, golau, Naddo; ceiniog, drud, ffair, prynu, pum, tri pheth) and the Pennod 9 words byw, sych, eich, marchog.

Applied from the Codex review (2026-10-12): s033 'Nac ydyn' answering 'Ydyn nhw'n gwerthu …?'; s121 'a dan y bwrdd' rewritten 'ac wedyn dan y bwrdd' rather than the reviewer's (correct) 'a than y bwrdd', to avoid a one-off tan/dan aspirate form the learner has no way to parse; B.b3 'Mae'r bluen'; feminine/far table cell now 'y llwy yna' (ymbarél is masculine); s027, B.b9 and C.c2 'dangos yr amser' instead of the calque 'cyfrif yr amser' (B.b9 counting sequence removed; dangos gloss and introduction moved from s085 to s027, its first use); A.a10 accepts Gwnes i and the ddoe cue; B.b7 accepts deall, B.b10 bocs; C.c2 'Oriawr yw hon', C.c3 the named-subject sentence.

primary_new_grammar.label: demonstratives: hwn / hon (this one, by gender), hwnnw / honno (that one, further off), y … yma / y … yna, y rhain (these ones), dyna (+ SM); hyn / hynny used separately: after a plural noun (y pethau hyn / hynny) and abstract (Beth yw hyn? Dw i ddim yn deall hynny)

cover.alt: Myrddin's dim tower on a rainy day: rain drips onto the books, a heavy leather-strapped chest stands shut, and Arth, Mali and Cai search among the shelves and the table of curiosities for the lost key while Myrddin holds up a candle.
cover.art_brief: Inside Myrddin's crooked grey stone tower (tower palette: grey stone, ink blue) on a dark rainy day: rain drips from the old roof beams onto a pile of books on the floor. Crowded shelves, a long table and a tall wooden cupboard with its door just ajar (the curved handle of a long black closed umbrella shows inside); a big wooden chest bound with leather straps, lid shut, against the wall; a black cauldron by the small hearth. On the table and shelves: a round silver pocket watch with a chain, a small hand mirror, white quills and a clay ink pot, a spare pair of round wire spectacles, a small wooden wheel and a big round button. Myrddin (very old, thin, long white beard, round wire spectacles, patched deep-blue robe, tall black brimmed hat) holds up a lit candle, puzzled; Dafi (cup-sized red dragon) peeps from his hat brim. Arth (11, untidy brown hair with cowlick, oversized moss-green tunic) peers under the table, Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress) searches a shelf, Cai (15, tall, ginger-blond, rust-red tunic) picks up a quill. Pero lies by the green door. No text.

grammar.nodyn_en: This one: hwn (masculine), hon (feminine); that one (further off): hwnnw, honno. With a noun: y bocs yma 'this box', y bocs yna 'that box'. These: y rhain. Hyn and hynny are for ideas (Beth yw hyn? 'What is this?') and after plural nouns (y pethau hyn). Dyna points: Dyna'r allwedd!
